title: Acoustic recording horns and the day-long 'I Can't Give You Anything But Love' with Armstr
summary: Early recording used horns, and the Louis Armstrong date spent half a day on a single melody-backing number before 'Mahogany Hall Stomp' the next day.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: But the records are true to what the band sounded like.
Oh yeah. Sure. Of course, in them days, there was not the high fidelity that they have nowadays, you know what I mean, in recording...

Recording was altogether different. Some of them numbers we recorded were done in the horns in the studio. You played in a big horn. You had a whole lot of horns around, and you played in the horn. There wasn't no microphones or anything. There wasn't no electric recording like that.

And the recording was not easy in them days either. I know that number we did with Louis Armstrong, and it was nothin' but a simple number, 'I Can't Give You Anything But Love' -- we played nothing but the melody in back of Louis. That recording taken us a half-a-day. And we were doin' nothin'. The band was doin' nothin'. But they were so technical down there about Louis, you know. All they wanted was Louis this, Louis... And they were so technical about that recording... That's the only thing we recorded that day -- that one number. The date was gone. Then we come back
again the next day and made some more numbers. We recorded the "Mahogany Hall Stomp" and all that stuff.

Recording was altogether different. Then when they come back later with this tape recording, boy, that was a breeze. But see, I wasn't with Louis' band then, or Russell's band. When they had this tape recording... We weren't recording at that time; let's put it like that.
